nodes.content: Design a mixed-criticality accelerator runtime guaranteeing control-task deadlines despite nonpreemptible inference kernels and shared-memory interference.
requirements: Under declared execution and interference bounds, all admitted control jobs meet 2 ms deadlines.
Guarantee starvation-free inference progress under adversarial arrivals without compromising admitted control deadlines.

nodes.content: Admit controls against 2-ms response bounds accounting for reserved FIFO inference slots, bounded nonpreemptible kernels, and shared-memory interference.
What positive inference-slot reservation preserves 2-ms control response bounds under worst-case arrivals and shared-memory interference?
Reserving 200 µs every 8 ms for ≤200-µs FIFO kernels, within interference-aware admission, preserves 2-ms deadlines and inference progress.
Derive interference-aware 2-ms control-response and FIFO service bounds for 200-µs slots every 8 ms under adversarial arrivals.
Compute control response and FIFO service bounds under adversarial arrivals, 200-µs/8-ms slots, 200-µs blocking, and 80-µs/job DRAM stalls.
A 200-µs kernel plus a permitted 80-µs DRAM stall needs 280 µs; strict 200-µs slots provide zero worst-case FIFO service.
Reserve 280-µs FIFO slots every 8 ms for 200-µs kernels plus 80-µs stalls; admit controls against blocking and interference.
Recalculate 2-ms control-response and FIFO-service bounds for 280-µs slots every 8 ms, including the 80-µs stall that invalidated 200-µs slots.
At ≤1.36-ms interference-inclusive control demand, 280-µs slot plus 280-µs blocking yields 1.92-ms response; backlogged FIFO completes ≥1 kernel/8 ms.
Adopt 280-µs slots every 8 ms and ≤1.36-ms control admission; rejected 200-µs slots cannot cover interference stalls.
SlotGuard specification: 280-µs FIFO slots every 8 ms, ≤1.36-ms control admission, 1.92-ms response bound, and backlogged FIFO service proof.
Implement SlotGuard trace simulator from its specification; replay adversarial arrivals and 80-µs stalls, checking 2-ms deadlines and FIFO progress.
SlotGuard adversarial traces recorded 1.92-ms maximum control response and one FIFO completion per reserved 8-ms cycle under continuous backlog.
Which hardware isolation and admission checks can enforce SlotGuard’s 80-µs DRAM-stall and 280-µs kernel bounds?
Configure DRAM QoS and tiled kernels; test adversarial contention against 200-µs execution and 80-µs stall limits before admission.
In QoSStress-1’s million launches, tiled kernels peaked at 198 µs execution and 76 µs DRAM stall under adversarial contention.
Adopt QoS-isolated tiled kernels conditionally: QoSStress-1 stayed within bounds and SlotGuard traces met deadlines; require certified bounds before admission.
Implement QoS-backed SlotGuard with certified kernel bounds, ≤1.36-ms control admission, 280-µs FIFO slots every 8 ms, and adversarial validation.
Partition accelerator into dedicated control and inference slices with guaranteed DRAM bandwidth; admit controls using interference-aware response-time analysis.
Can hardware-sliced control and inference lanes sustain independent progress while DRAM contention remains bounded within 2-ms control deadlines?
With 75/25 compute slices and 70/30 DRAM guarantees, ≤1.5-ms interference-inclusive control demand meets deadlines; inference completes ≥1 kernel/8 ms.
Using SlotGuard’s kernel bounds, simulate 75/25 compute and 70/30 DRAM slices under adversarial 1.5-ms demand; check deadlines and inference progress.
SliceSim-A recorded 1.78-ms maximum control response and ≥1 inference completion per 8-ms cycle under backlog and adversarial contention.
Use SlotGuard’s 280-µs kernel bound in a hardware contention microbenchmark to verify 70/30 DRAM guarantees and independent slice dispatch.
SliceBench-H: 75/25 compute and verified 70/30 DRAM still incurred 610-µs shared-dispatch blocking; 1.5-ms controls responded in 2.11 ms.
Independent per-slice queues with ≤100-µs dispatch blocking should yield ≤1.6-ms control response and ≥1 inference completion/8 ms.
Implement independent per-slice dispatch queues; replay SliceSim-A arrivals on SliceBench-H using SlotGuard bounds; measure blocking, response, inference throughput.
SliceBench-H with per-slice queues measured 92-µs maximum dispatch blocking, 1.592-ms control response, and ≥1 inference completion/8 ms.
Derive arrival-curve admission and inference-service proofs using SlotGuard kernel bounds; verify 100-µs per-slice dispatch cap against SliceBench-H traces.
Arrival-curve analysis permits three simultaneous 500-µs controls; three 100-µs dispatch delays yield 1.8-ms response, refuting the 1.6-ms bound.
Arrival-curve admission charging 100-µs dispatch per control job should prove ≤2-ms responses; the independent inference slice sustains ≥1 kernel/8 ms.
Derive arrival-curve admission and inference-service bounds with per-job 100-µs dispatch, SliceBench-H isolation, and SlotGuard’s 280-µs kernels.
Arrival-curve proof bounds admitted controls at 1.8 ms including per-job dispatch; the isolated inference slice guarantees ≥1 kernel/8 ms.
Adopt per-slice queues and per-job 100-µs dispatch admission: measured blocking is 92 µs; corrected control bound is 1.8 ms.
Implement 75/25 slices, 70/30 DRAM QoS, per-slice queues, and arrival-curve admission charging 100 µs dispatch per control.
Implement 75/25 slices, 70/30 DRAM QoS, and per-slice queues; stress-test SlotGuard-bounded admission charging 100-µs dispatch under adversarial arrivals.
SliceGuard v0.1: 75/25 compute slices, 70/30 DRAM QoS, per-slice queues, 100-µs dispatch admission charges, and adversarial test logs.
SliceGuard v0.1 stress logs showed 1.79-ms maximum admitted-control response and ≥1 inference completion per backlogged 8-ms cycle.
Select SliceGuard’s isolated slices for deployment: corrected admission proves 1.8-ms control response, and stress logs show inference progress.
Use hierarchical EDF with a 10%-reserved inference server, ≤150-µs interference-bounded kernel tiles, and control admission accounting for server interference.
What 10% server period and budget cover 150-µs tiles plus 80-µs DRAM stalls while preserving admitted 2-ms EDF deadlines?
A 240-µs/2.4-ms FIFO server fits 150-µs tiles plus 80-µs stalls; interference-aware EDF admission preserves deadlines and progress.
Replay SliceGuard v0.1 adversarial logs with 80-µs stalls; analyze 240-µs/2.4-ms server EDF deadlines and FIFO tile service.
SliceGuard replay exposed 92-µs launch delay: a 150-µs tile plus 80-µs stall needs 322 µs, exceeding 240-µs server budget.
Run hierarchical EDF on SliceGuard v0.1 hardware with adversarial control releases; log deadline misses and FIFO service at 240-µs budgets.
In sampled runs with ≤8-µs launch delays, EDF peaked at 1.94-ms control response and completed ≥1 FIFO tile/period.
Reject 240-µs server certification: sampled 8-µs launches pass, but permitted 92-µs delays prevent worst-case tile service.
Evaluate a 330-µs/3.3-ms server covering 322-µs worst-case tiles; recompute EDF admission and FIFO service under adversarial arrivals.
Replay SliceGuard v0.1 adversarial traces with 330-µs/3.3-ms budgets; calculate EDF response and FIFO service under 92-µs launch delays.
EDF-Server-330 report contains adversarial replay traces, response-time calculations, and FIFO-service analysis for 330-µs budgets every 3.3 ms.
EDF-Server-330 analysis bounds admitted control response at 1.98 ms and backlogged FIFO service at ≥1 tile/3.3 ms under 92-µs launches.
Implement EDF-Server-330 on hardware; inject 92-µs launch delays and adversarial control arrivals, measuring deadline response and FIFO progress.
EDF-Server-330 hardware hit 2.04-ms control response with 92-µs launches; unmodeled 60-µs replenishment jitter broke admission.
Defer hierarchical EDF: the 330-µs server’s 1.98-ms bound omits jitter causing 2.04-ms misses; 240-µs budgets lack guaranteed progress.
Retain the 330-µs/3.3-ms server; tighten EDF admission for 60-µs replenishment jitter and reprove bounded FIFO service.
Recompute EDF-Server-330 admission with 60-µs replenishment jitter; verify revised control and FIFO bounds against 92-µs-launch hardware traces.
EDF-Server-330-J report adds 60-µs jitter to admission tests, control-response bounds, and backlogged FIFO service calculations.
EDF-Server-330-J bounds admitted responses at 1.96 ms including jitter; hardware traces peaked at 1.95 ms with ≥1 tile/3.36 ms.
Adopt jitter-aware EDF-Server-330 with tightened admission: 1.96-ms control response and ≥1 backlogged FIFO tile/3.36 ms resolve prior failures.
